step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard diagram illustrates Alef Education's personalized e-learning recommendation system. 1. External actors include Students (120k) and Authors. 2. Students generate learning event data sent to S3 (100M data points) and access the platform via ELB leading to an inference EKS cluster. 3. Authors send content/authoring events (65k data points) directly to Redshift. 4. Unstructured data in S3 is processed into Redshift (3TB consolidated warehouse). 5. Consolidated Redshift data flows into a training EKS cluster running Kubeflow, which interfaces with SageMaker for hyperparameter tuning. 6. The best trained model is packaged into Docker builds and stored in ECR. 7. Models from ECR are deployed into the inference EKS cluster for student recommendations. 8. CloudWatch is drawn as a standalone monitoring component on the diagram with no direct explicit line arrows attached to it.
